name: Radium-223 dichloride (symptomatic bone-predominant mCRPC)

institution.provenance: ONCOTREE draft protocol authored from standard-of-care oncology knowledge (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Radium-223 is an alpha-emitting bone-seeking radiopharmaceutical for symptomatic bone-predominant mCRPC without visceral metastases; it prolongs survival and delays symptomatic skeletal events. It is not combined with abiraterone plus prednisone. Continue ADT to maintain castrate testosterone.

stage: M1 CRPC (metastatic castration-resistant, symptomatic bone metastases, no visceral disease)
supportiveCare: Continue ADT to keep testosterone below 50 ng/dL; add a bone-modifying agent (denosumab or zoledronic acid) for skeletal-event prevention.
Do not co-administer with abiraterone plus prednisone (increased fracture / death risk in that combination).
Administer by a licensed nuclear-medicine facility with radiation-safety precautions; six injections at 4-week intervals.
monitoring: CBC before each injection (hold for neutropenia or thrombocytopenia)
PSA and serum testosterone (confirm castrate level)

doseModificationRules.text: Hold until recovery and obtain hematologic review; discontinue if counts do not recover within the labeled interval. Physician decides.

drugs.name: Radium-223 dichloride
drugs.notes: Weight-based radioactivity: 55 kBq/kg IV as a slow injection on day 1, repeated every 4 weeks for 6 injections. UNIT NOTE: the dose is radioactivity per body weight (kBq/kg), not milligrams; the engine multiplies 55 by patient weight to give the per-injection activity in kBq. Alpha-emitter, no ISMP tall-man form; administer under nuclear-medicine radiation-safety protocol. Dose reflects standard radium-223 practice (general reference).
